svg.title: Layers and attention heads
svg.text: 3 · Inside a layer: twelve heads, each reading the sentence differently
Real attention weights for the sentence above. Each row sums to 1 — a head spreads one unit of attention.
reads the word immediately before — every time
reaches across the sentence to a related word
Heads specialise, but most of them are not doing anything tidy.
56 of the 144 send over 70% of their attention to punctuation and sentence markers — a known idling behaviour. Only 16 mostly read the words.
A head is a 64-number slice of the 768: twelve of them, each attending independently, then joined back together. 12 × 64 = 768.
A layer is one round of that. Stacking twelve means a token can be influenced by a word it never looked at directly — reached through
whatever the layer below already folded in.
